evals.prompt: Draft a Jira story from this early request before any plan or SDD exists. Capture the as-is problem, to-be outcome, scope, guidance, acceptance, and open questions. Do not create planning artifacts or pretend the ticket is ready if a material decision is missing.
evals.expected_output: Produces a copy-ready intake ticket with a summary, issue type, concise description, honest readiness state, and no new plan/spec/design/tasks files.
expectations: Treats the ticket as intake rather than a hidden SDD artifact
Includes as-is, to-be, in/out scope, acceptance, and open questions
Does not create or modify planning or SDD artifacts

evals.prompt: Using the existing plan, formal SDD artifacts, and ADR, compose a compact Jira story for the same change. Keep the ticket self-contained for execution but link the deeper artifacts instead of copying their full detail or architectural rationale.
evals.expected_output: Produces a concise ticket payload with current state, outcome, scope, only relevant guidance, acceptance, verification, dependencies, and references to the plan/SDD artifacts; the source artifacts remain unchanged.
expectations: Uses artifacts as source material without making the ticket a full design document
Preserves the distinction between ticket summary and formal artifact detail
Includes useful references and does not invent missing links
Links architectural rationale through the ADR without duplicating its alternatives or tradeoffs

evals.prompt: Review this long Jira ticket that contains the entire design history and a full implementation checklist. Make it shorter without losing the as-is problem, to-be outcome, scope, guidance, acceptance, verification, or references.
evals.expected_output: Reports overlong or misplaced detail, proposes a compact replacement description, and moves full rationale/history/checklist detail into references rather than deleting necessary execution context.
expectations: Keeps execution-critical context in the ticket
Removes or links detailed alternatives and route history
Does not silently change the requested outcome

evals.prompt: Decide whether this large change should remain one story ticket with subtasks or become multiple sibling tickets. The work has one user outcome but several implementation owners and phases.
evals.expected_output: Keeps one parent story when the acceptance boundary and outcome are shared, drafts bounded subtasks with their own acceptance and verification, and explains when a sibling ticket would instead be warranted.
expectations: Does not equate an Epic with the SDD change or parent story
Uses subtasks for implementation decomposition within one outcome
Checks independent outcome, priority, release, owner, and acceptance signals

evals.prompt: An existing ticket now has a plan, design ADR, and SDD change. Add only verified references and a concise context note to the ticket. Do not edit any of those artifacts and do not publish to Jira.
evals.expected_output: Produces a minimal ticket update payload containing verified artifact references, leaves the artifacts unchanged, and clearly says that no external Jira update occurred.
expectations: Treats the ticket as a pointer to artifacts rather than a contributor to them
Does not invent paths or links
Stops at a copy-ready update without external publication

evals.prompt: The user asks my-planning to turn a plan into a Jira ticket. Route the request to the ticket-specific workflow instead of creating local ticket files or changing the plan.
evals.expected_output: Explains that my-ticket owns ticket drafting/refinement, passes the plan as reference context, and preserves the plan and SDD artifact boundaries.
expectations: Does not add ticket.md under docs/change
Does not treat ticket creation as a planning artifact operation
Keeps external publication explicit and unauthorized by default

evals.prompt: Draft a GitHub issue for a repository that has not configured GitHub issue types and where the user supplied no labels, milestone, or project. Include the issue title and a compact body with acceptance and verification. Do not publish or invent tracker fields.
evals.expected_output: Produces a copy-ready GitHub issue title and Markdown body, treats the type as a suggestion rather than an unsupported native field, and does not claim an issue was created.
expectations: Supports GitHub Issues as a target alongside Jira
Maps summary and execution context to issue title and body
Does not invent issue types, labels, milestones, projects, or links
Does not publish without an explicit request and configured integration

evals.prompt: The user explicitly asks to publish a GitHub issue, but no GitHub integration or authorized tool is configured. Prepare the issue payload and clearly state that it was not published.
evals.expected_output: Returns a copy-ready GitHub issue title and body, identifies the missing integration as the blocker, and makes no claim of external creation.
expectations: Recognizes GitHub Issues as supported for drafting
Requires an actually configured and authorized integration for publishing
Reports that no external issue was created
